scenarios.title: Submit a valid manuscript to an available publishing package and receive confirmation and reduced seat availability
scenarios.intent: Prove that a complete valid submission succeeds, returns the authored confirmation details and reference, and reduces the package's shared remaining seat count by one.
scenarios.technique_notes: Techniques: Equivalence partitioning for a valid complete field set; CRUD round-trip for the persisted submission write; State / flow for submit-and-return behavior. Risk judged high because money and shared-capacity rules apply, so this write path was retained first under max_pairs=3.

scenarios.title: Submit a manuscript with a stale or unoffered onboarding seat and receive the seat-unavailable rejection
scenarios.intent: Prove that a seat value that is no longer available or was never offered is rejected with the seat-unavailable message and no successful submission.
scenarios.technique_notes: Techniques: Negative / error for rejected submission; Equivalence partitioning across two invalid seat classes that share one expected outcome. Risk judged high because a stale or forged seat can overbook shared monthly capacity on a priced package, so this path was retained under max_pairs=3.

scenarios.title: Open a fully booked publishing package detail page and see the booked message instead of a submission form
scenarios.intent: Prove that a package with no seats left suppresses the submission form and shows the fully booked message on its detail page.
scenarios.technique_notes: Techniques: Boundary value analysis on the zero-seats-left boundary; Negative / error because the user must be blocked from starting a submission; Persistence of the shared-capacity state in the rendered package detail page. Risk judged high because this terminal capacity state prevents futile submissions and misleading availability claims.

gaps.risk_rationale: This gap ranked lowest because it is a single-field validation outcome and is less likely to cause revenue or capacity loss than the retained success and seat-capacity paths.

judgements.rationale: Highest value: this is the revenue-bearing primary path and the only path that proves submission creation, authored confirmation content, and the shared seat-count decrement after a write.
Very high value: it protects the shared monthly-capacity rule against stale or forged seat values, which would otherwise oversubscribe a priced package.
High value: it proves the terminal capacity boundary where the form must be suppressed entirely, preventing futile or misleading submission attempts.
Useful but lower than capacity rules under the budget: required-field validation is explicit and important, but it does not protect shared inventory or the successful paid-intent path.
Useful but lowest under the budget: manuscript-status validation is a single-field negative distinct from the more consequential inventory and success paths.
Applied happy-path, equivalence-partition, CRUD, and state-flow techniques because the use case creates a persisted submission and returns to the package page with a changed shared-capacity state.
Applied negative and equivalence-partition techniques because two invalid seat classes share one rejection outcome and both threaten the same capacity rule.
Applied boundary and negative techniques because zero remaining seats is the explicit terminal limit where the submission surface must be suppressed.
Applied negative and equivalence-partition techniques because each missing required field should lead to the same rejection and no-creation outcome; budget later evicted it.
Applied negative technique because leaving manuscript status at its default prompt should block submission with a distinct error message; budget later evicted it.
